title: Inference on Quantile Treatment Effects with Small Treatment Groups
abstract: arXiv:2105.10965v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We develop inference for conditional quantile treatment effects that allows treatment groups to remain small as the overall sample grows. Such groups arise naturally in multivalued treatment models. Our procedure combines estimation of a conditional quantile function from a large reference group with an exact conditional Bernoulli representation of quantile indicators. We establish asymptotic size control and derive a power bound allowing treatment-group sizes to remain bounded. The framework accommodates nonseparable outcome functions, heteroskedasticity, and flexible error distributions across treatment profiles. We illustrate its scope through dynamic treatment models, nonseparable quantile models, and difference-in-differences designs with staggered adoption. Monte Carlo experiments assess finite-sample performance, and an application to temperature shocks and GDP growth illustrates inference on effects associated with distinct t

translated_title: 处理组规模较小时分位数处理效应的推断
translated_abstract: 我们针对条件分位数处理效应发展了一种统计推断方法，该方法允许处理组在总样本增长时仍保持较小规模。这类小处理组自然出现在多值处理模型中。我们的方法将来自大参考组的条件分位数函数估计与分位数指标的精确条件伯努利表示相结合。我们建立了渐近水平控制，并推导出功效界，且允许处理组规模保持有界。该框架适用于不可分离的结果函数、异方差性以及跨处理组合的灵活误差分布。我们通过动态处理模型、不可分离分位数模型以及交错采纳的双重差分设计来说明该方法的适用范围。蒙特卡洛实验评估了有限样本下的表现，而对温度冲击与GDP增长的应用则展示了对不同温度水平相关效应的推断。
tldr: 本文提出了一种在总样本增长时处理组规模仍可保持有界（较小）的情况下对条件分位数处理效应进行有效统计推断的新方法，该方法结合大参考组的条件分位数函数估计与分位数指标的精确条件伯努利表示，实现了渐近水平控制和功效保证，并可应用于动态处理模型、不可分离分位数模型及交错采纳的双重差分设计。
en_tdlr: This paper develops inference for conditional quantile treatment effects that remains valid when treatment groups stay small (even bounded) as the sample grows, by combining conditional quantile function estimation from a large reference group with an exact conditional Bernoulli representation of quantile indicators, achieving asymptotic size control and power guarantees, with applications to dynamic treatment models, nonseparable quantile models, and staggered difference-in-differences designs.
